methodological_rigor.justification: The phase I open-label dose-escalation/expansion design with a 28-day DLT window is appropriate for the primary safety/tolerability/PK aims, and combining Parts I and J is justified because both received the identical 75 mg camizestrant + 400 mg capivasertib (4d on/3d off) regimen. The sample size (n = 29) is small but adequate for a phase I design; no formal power calculation is reported, which is expected. Statistical methods are appropriate: Clopper-Pearson exact 95% CIs for ORR, Kaplan-Meier for PFS, descriptive summaries for AEs and PK, and within-participant comparisons (C1D18 vs C2D1) for the DDI question. Limitations are explicitly acknowledged (open-label single-arm, small cohort, incomplete PTEN-loss detection by the ctDNA assays), but subgroup efficacy splits (ESR1m, PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN) rely on very small cells (as small as 11-17) without multiplicity adjustment and should be interpreted cautiously.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a non-randomized, single-arm phase I dose-escalation/expansion trial (n = 29) with no internal comparator, mapping to Oxford CEBM level 4 (early-phase case series / low-quality cohort for therapeutic claims). Clinical relevance is nonetheless high: it provides the first safety, PK (showing no clinically meaningful drug-drug interaction) and preliminary efficacy data for pairing a next-generation oral SERD (camizestrant) with an AKT inhibitor (capivasertib) in a heavily pretreated ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer population, directly motivating a phase III test of this fulvestrant-sparing backbone. Endpoints (CBR24, ORR, PFS) are standard surrogates for this disease context and the median PFS of 8.3 months is clinically interpretable given 55% prior fulvestrant and 90% prior CDK4/6i exposure.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT (with phase I/early-phase extension considerations) is the applicable standard. The manuscript reports trial registration (NCT03616587), eligibility, dose rationale, DLT definitions, central ECG and PK sampling schedules, CTCAE v4.03 grading, pre-specified endpoints, enrollment dates, and a disposition reference (Supplementary Figure S1), with Tables 1-2 covering baseline characteristics and AE frequencies. Omissions include a visible CONSORT flow diagram in the main text, formal multiplicity handling for subgroup analyses, and explicit protocol-amendment history. Data/code availability is weak: the blinded manuscript contains no public repository deposit, no data-sharing statement visible in the main text, and no analytic code reference-only redacted URLs for supplementary materials remain.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first clinical report, to the manuscript's knowledge, of the specific combination of camizestrant (next-generation oral SERD) with capivasertib (pan-AKT inhibitor) in ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer, representing a meaningful but incremental extension of prior SERENA-1 (monotherapy, CDK4/6i combinations) and CAPItello-291 (capivasertib + fulvestrant) programs. Novelty is primarily empirical/combinational rather than conceptual or mechanistic: both agents are well-characterized, and the preclinical rationale for SERD + PI3K/AKT/mTOR combinations was already established (ref 8). The paper locates itself credibly in the SERENA and CAPItello literature without overclaiming.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well-organized, with a self-contained abstract that quantitatively summarizes safety (diarrhea 75.9%, nausea 44.8%), PK (tmax ~4 h for camizestrant, ~2 h for capivasertib), and efficacy (CBR24 51.7%, mPFS 8.3 months). Introduction places the combination in context of SERENA-2, SERENA-6, and CAPItello-291; methods, results, and discussion follow a logical flow without excessive repetition. Figure and table captions are informative and standalone-interpretable, including footnotes clarifying data-set definitions and assay limitations. Minor issues: 'stimulations' appears where 'simulations' is meant in Figure 1 and in the PK text, and some AE sentences could be tightened.

key_strengths: First clinical safety/PK/efficacy report of camizestrant + capivasertib combination with clear phase III-enabling implications in ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer

Pre-specified phase I design with DLT window, appropriate descriptive statistics, Clopper-Pearson ORR CIs, Kaplan-Meier PFS, and within-participant PK comparisons showing no clinically relevant drug-drug interaction
Transparent acknowledgement of limitations including open-label single-arm design, small sample, and incomplete PTEN-loss detection by the ctDNA assays used
ctDNA pharmacodynamic readout (ESR1m clearance in 67% to undetectable, >=50% reduction in 92%) adds mechanistic support to the efficacy signal
Clear, well-structured writing with informative tables, captions, and a quantitatively grounded abstract
key_concerns: Subgroup efficacy analyses (ESR1m, PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN) rest on very small cells (n = 11-17) with no multiplicity correction and should be framed as exploratory
No visible CONSORT flow diagram in main text and limited protocol/amendment transparency; data-sharing and code availability are not addressed in the blinded manuscript
Non-randomized, open-label design precludes causal attribution of efficacy to the combination over either monotherapy
Typographical issue: 'stimulations' used in place of 'simulations' in PK text and Figure 1 legend

Capivasertib exposure (Cmax +47%, AUC +25%) numerically higher than CAPItello-291 pop-PK; the manuscript asserts no clinically relevant DDI but a more rigorous quantitative DDI assessment would strengthen the claim
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically sound, well-written phase I combination trial with clinically meaningful signal and clean reporting; novelty is empirical/combinational rather than paradigm-shifting, placing it at tier 2 (strong specialty oncology journals) with minor revisions warranted for subgroup framing, DDI quantification, and reporting-standard gaps.
